Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (US, UK, Germany, France, Japan, EU)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Global bond yields are at or near multi-decade highs across the US, UK, Germany, France and Japan, driven by persistent inflation, renewed oil price pressures from US-Iran tensions, surging government debt loads, and massive AI-related corporate bond issuance. Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech has reinforced rate hike expectations. Bond vigilantes remain active; durable yield relief requires either credible fiscal consolidation or stronger growth across major economies.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (US is the primary anchor of the article, though the selloff is framed globally)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly skewed toward higher-for-longer and further hike expectations)
Probability of increase: 70%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (minimal treatment; Treasury buybacks briefly stabilized markets but yields resumed climbing)
Probability of holding: 20%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (cuts not meaningfully discussed; only conditional long-term relief if fiscal discipline is restored)
Probability of decrease: 10%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (Distinctly hawkish — Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, renewed oil-driven inflation, record corporate issuance, and $40T US debt pile all point toward sustained upward yield pressure with no near-term catalyst for easing)
